# judgment

> Typed, calibrated judgments from TypeSafe System One models (Jev) and compatible backends, as a Rust crate and the jud command line.

This index is generated from the crate's documentation nav (`mkdocs.yml`) and each page's frontmatter by `scripts/gen-llms-txt.sh`; the pages are the source of truth. The documentation follows Diátaxis: Start holds the tutorials (install, a first decision from the command line, a first decision in Rust), Guides the tasks (a backend, a rubric, cases, recordings, thresholds, CI, the container, the plugin, the patterns), Reference the facts (the jud command generated from its own help, the configuration, the normative .jud format specification, the crate's features and modules, the container image, stability, the glossary), Concepts the why (System One, rubrics, cases and recordings, how judgment works), and Project what is about the repository (contributing, internals, releasing, what real servers did, research, decisions). The rustdoc is the reference for every type, at https://docs.rs/judgment (or `cargo doc --open`). The crate has been run against the hosted TypeSafe API (`jev-1.13.0`), Laya's open-weights server and Ollama; its retry behaviour on 408, 429 and 529 is verified against wiremock only.

## Start

- [Install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/start/install.md): Every way to get the jud command and the judgment crate: mise, Homebrew, a release tarball with its checksum and attestation, cargo-binstall, cargo install, the container image, the crate as a dependency with its features, and shell completion.
- [Your first decision from the command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/start/first-decision-cli.md): From nothing to a verdict with the jud command and no account, by replaying a recorded answer; then the same command against the hosted API or a local model.
- [Your first decision in Rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/start/first-decision-rust.md): From an empty crate to a decision made on a model's answers, in Rust, with no account; first against the Fake backend, then the same decision from a .jud rubric, then against the hosted API with a key.

## Guides

- [Configure a backend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/configure-a-backend.md): How to point the jud command, the examples and the crate's client at the hosted TypeSafe API, at Ollama on your machine, at laya-serve, at Clef on Workers AI, at any other server that speaks the wire, or at a model on Google Cloud; and what each local server does differently from the hosted API.
- [Write a rubric](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/write-a-rubric.md): How to write a .jud Rubric from a brief, question by question, with a policy that is honest about its numbers, and check it with the crate's reader before it is used.
- [Label cases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/label-cases.md): How to write the labelled cases a rubric is graded on and its thresholds are tuned from, bind them to the rubric, and check that every label fits the request its case lowers to.
- [Record, replay and test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/record-replay-and-test.md): How to test a decision with no key and no network, with the Fake backend that refuses an answer the question could not produce, the Recorder and Replay pair keyed by the request's content, jud --replay for a rubric on the command line, and jud record to answer a rubric's labelled cases once and keep the answers.
- [Tune thresholds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/tune-thresholds.md): How to grade a model's recorded answers against a rubric's labelled cases with jud eval, hold them to an accuracy bar that fails CI, and replace the guessed bars of the policy with bars proposed by jud tune from a table, then write them back with their provenance.
- [Run in CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/run-in-ci.md): How to check every .jud document in a repository, replay a smoke case with no key, fail a job when a model's recorded answers no longer meet the labels with jud eval and its exit status 3, and run a rubric with a key in a CI job, with the binary installed or as the container image, and how to read the exit status in a script.
- [Run in a container](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/run-in-a-container.md): How to run jud as the ghcr.io/chussenot/jud image: how a rubric and a state reach it through the working directory and stdin, what the non-root user without a shell changes, and the four ways a backend is reached from inside, a key, another server, the host's Ollama, a replay directory.
- [Use the Claude Code plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/use-the-claude-code-plugin.md): How to install the jud plugin from this repository's marketplace, write a rubric and its cases with /jud:rubric and /jud:cases, check them with /jud:check, and measure and tune them with /jud:record, /jud:eval and /jud:tune, and turn a rubric into a typed Rust module with /jud:rust; what the three skills know that the reader and the numbers cannot say.
- [Patterns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/guides/patterns.md): TypeSafe's four patterns, speculative fan-out, confidence-gated routing, composite scoring and intent routing, mapped onto the crate's types, with one runnable example each that replays committed recordings and three things the recordings teach about thresholds.

## Reference

- [The jud command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/cli.md): Every command, flag, argument and environment variable of the jud binary, with each command's help text as the binary prints it, the verdict JSON a run writes, the report jud eval prints and its JSON keys, what jud record, jud tune and jud split write, and the exit status.
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every setting the jud command and the crate's client read, where each comes from, in what order of precedence, and what the defaults are; the configuration file's fields, the output of jud config, and which commands read JUD_REPLAY.
- [The .jud format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/jud-format.md): The normative specification of apiVersion jud/v1.3, the YAML document format for a rubric with its policy, the labelled cases it is graded on and the recordings of what a model answered, in a manifest envelope with content fingerprints any implementation computes the same way.
- [The crate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/crate.md): The judgment crate as a dependency; its features and what each compiles, its modules with a link to the rustdoc of each, the error groups, the limits and the defaults.
- [The container image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/container-image.md): What is inside ghcr.io/chussenot/jud, the user it runs as, the paths it reads, the tags a release pushes, and how its provenance is verified.
- [Stability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/stability.md): What stays the same across versions and for how long, so a document, a recording or a dependency written today keeps working; the jud/v1 format is stable, a minor version only adds, a reader accepts every v1 document for at least twelve months after a later minor is published, fingerprints exclude the envelope and never change for a document's spec, the jud command's exit status, JSON output and file writes are a contract, and the crate's 0.x releases say what they break.
- [Glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/reference/glossary.md): The terms the documentation uses, each defined once, with the page that owns it.

## Concepts

- [System One](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/concepts/system-one.md): What a System One model answers, why a calibrated probability suits a decision better than generated text, and the three primitives (Noul, Choice, Score) with what each returns.
- [Rubrics, cases and recordings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/concepts/rubrics-cases-recordings.md): Why a decision is written as a rubric, why the labelled examples it is graded on and the answers a model gave are documents of their own, how the three name each other by content, and the loop that tunes a policy from them.
- [How judgment works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/concepts/how-judgment-works.md): The mechanisms behind the crate's guarantees, typed handles from a question to its answer, the response check every backend applies, the path of one call through the modules, the retry loop with the official SDKs' defaults, the error grouping and the request id, and what the crate deliberately does not do.

## Project

- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/contributing.md): How the repository is worked on; the quality gates and the hooks, tracking work in beads, Conventional Commits, how the documentation is organised (Diátaxis) and checked, what is generated, how the container image is built locally, and how a decision is recorded.
- [Internals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/internals.md): The rules the code applies that the rustdoc states only once, with the reason behind each; the client's key check, status classification and error-body reading, the per-call options, the retry loop's edges, the backends, the tolerant decoder, what the response check leaves unchecked, the observer, the recordings and metrics, the .jud reader, and the bounded proofs.
- [Releasing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/releasing.md): How a version of the judgment crate is cut from its Conventional Commits with cocogitto, how the pushed tag publishes it to crates.io, the jud binaries to a GitHub release, the Homebrew formula to the tap and the container image to ghcr.io from CI, what to set up once, and what to do when a release goes wrong.

## Project: Verification

- [How the crate is checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/verification/method.md): The three checks that stand between the crate's mocks and a real server, the ignored live tests, the benchmark replay and the contract test against the vendored OpenAPI document, what each one can and cannot establish, and how to run them against the hosted API, Laya, Ollama or Clef on Workers AI.
- [Against the hosted TypeSafe API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/verification/hosted-typesafe.md): The judgment crate's live tests run against api.typesafe.ai with a real key, what each one showed about the hosted wire that the mocks and the Laya run could not, what probing past the builder's limits taught (three 400 shapes, the token budget, non-determinism at two decimals, the confidence formulas) and what the crate changed for it, and how to repeat the check with one task.
- [Against Laya typed-decisions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/verification/laya-typed-decisions.md): How the judgment crate was tested against Laya's typed-decisions checkpoint through laya-serve, what each test asserts and why, the decoding bug the first run caught, the benchmark numbers, the 2026-10-03 re-run against laya-serve 0.3.24 and the legend comparison it loosened, and how to repeat the run.

## Project: Research

- [System One client libraries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/research/system-one-client-libraries.md): A survey of the twenty-five community Rust clients for the TypeSafe System One wire, the official Python and JavaScript SDKs and the live OpenAPI document, what each did that judgment 0.1 did not, the ranked changes worth making to the crate, the ones rejected and why, and what judgment 0.2.0 shipped of them.
- [Compatible servers and models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/research/compatible-servers-and-models.md): The servers and models that speak the System One wire as of 2026-10-06, hosted and local, what the Jev Decision Index 0.2.1 says about how close the open ones are to Jev, what each one's limits and confidence semantics mean for a consumer of this crate, and which the crate has been run against or should be next.
- [Compared with the other Rust clients](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/research/client-comparison.md): A feature-by-feature comparison of judgment with the nine most-downloaded Rust crates for the System One wire, each read from its published source on 2026-10-04 and measured for dependency footprint and build time, in five grids (the wire, reading answers, resilience, testing and evaluation, observability and footprint), with what judgment should take from the others next.
- [System One models on Google Cloud](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/research/system-one-on-google-cloud.md): A study, as of 2026-10-06, of how a System One model can be reached on Google Cloud (a compatible server on Cloud Run, an open-weights model on a Vertex AI endpoint, a partner model on Model Garden, a gateway in front of the hosted API), what the crate's client already does for each path and where it stops (the request path, a short-lived bearer, the model list), and how a caller attaches request labels in an HTTP header with the client as it is, with the vendor's rules for them and the changes to the crate that would make a Vertex AI endpoint a base URL and nothing more.

## Project: Decisions

- [Decisions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/README.md): The architecture decision records that govern the judgment crate's design, how they are numbered, how a record is written, and what has moved since each was accepted.
- [0003 Typed handles between questions and answers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0003-typed-handles-between-questions-and-answers.md): Adding a question returns a handle that fixes the answer type, so the compiler ties each wire answer to the code that consumes it.
- [0013 Releases cut with cocogitto and published from CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0013-releases-cut-with-cocogitto-and-published-from-ci.md): The version is derived from Conventional Commits by cocogitto, the CHANGELOG stays hand-written, and a pushed tag runs the gate and publishes the crate to crates.io, so no release depends on one person's laptop or memory.
- [0014 A file format for rubrics, cases and recordings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0014-a-file-format-for-rubrics-cases-and-recordings.md): The questions a request sends, the policy that reads the answers, the labelled cases the policy is tuned on and the recordings of what a model answered get one YAML format, .jud, with the wire's own shapes, content fingerprints from RFC 8785 canonical JSON and strict reading, instead of staying in code, configuration and notebooks that drift apart.
- [0016 The .jud format takes minor versions, and 1.1 makes the request depend on the state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0016-jud-takes-minor-versions.md): The .jud format gains a minor version, 1.1, which only adds; it lets a rubric declare when a question or an instruction part is sent and that a Choice's options come with the request, lets a gate carry bands, a level threshold and strict comparison, and reserves top-level x- keys, so that a real application's questions and policy fit in the file.
- [0017 The .jud format 1.2 refuses what a reviewer cannot see, and names the policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0017-jud-1-2-refuses-what-a-reviewer-cannot-see.md): Version 1.2 of the .jud format adds no field; it makes every id a name that is never a path, refuses YAML merge keys and tags the core schema does not define, keeps a binary scalar as its text, keeps the document out of error messages, and gives a rubric's policy a fingerprint of its own, because a threat model found that a reviewed rubric could still read differently from how it looked and that the questions' fingerprint could not show a moved threshold.
- [0018 The .jud format 1.3 takes the manifest envelope and reads one apiVersion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0018-jud-1-3-takes-the-manifest-envelope.md): Version 1.3 of the .jud format moves its envelope to a Kubernetes manifest's (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec), so that people and tools that read manifests and Backstage catalog files read these, and its reader reads exactly one apiVersion, withdrawing the rule of 0016 that a minor version adds and a reader reads every earlier one; this record maps the earlier keys onto the new envelope and is the one page that names them.
- [0019 A command line for the format, released as a binary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0019-a-command-line-for-the-format.md): Why the jud binary evaluates stdin against a Rubric file rather than taking a bespoke input language, why its backend is the crate's client with TypeSafe as the default and a base URL as the only switch, why it reads a configuration file where the crate reads only the environment, and why it is released as one tarball per platform in the shape of pact's releases.
- [0020 How a v1 minor of the .jud format is spelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0020-how-a-v1-minor-is-spelled.md): Proposed and not applied; whether a minor version of the jud/v1 format stays in the apiVersion string (jud/v1.3, jud/v1.4) or moves to a field of its own under apiVersion jud/v1, now that the stability page promises that a minor only adds and that a reader accepts every v1 document for at least twelve months; each option priced in files rewritten, reader logic and what tools that key on apiVersion see.
- [0021 Record, evaluate and tune from the command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0021-record-eval-and-tune-from-the-command-line.md): Accepted and implemented; three jud subcommands close the loop from a rubric and its labelled cases to a tuned policy without Rust. jud record answers every case once and writes the recordings, jud eval grades answers against the labels and gates CI with a new exit status 3, and jud tune proposes bars from recordings only, printing them by default; why three commands rather than one, what each writes, what the implementation settled, and what the choice costs.
- [0022 jud reports what the tuning loop counted by hand](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0022-jud-reports-what-the-tuning-loop-counted-by-hand.md): Accepted and implemented; after a real-world run, three additions move into the jud command what the tuning skill and its users computed by hand. jud eval reports each question's answers by outcome, its majority label and its signals (no better than the majority, collapsed, an outcome never answered, a gate that defers most or nearly all) with the thresholds they were read with; jud record --dry-run says what a run would ask, of whom and for how long; jud split writes a tuning set and a held-out set, each case copied as read. Why the command and not the skill, the thresholds chosen, and what it costs.
- [0023 jud RUBRIC takes per-request options on the command line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chussenot/judgment/main/docs/project/decisions/0023-jud-rubric-takes-options-on-the-command-line.md): Why the options of a Choice marked options_from request reach jud RUBRIC through --options and --options-file rather than through the state on stdin or a path into it, which 0019 left for later and which tool choice, the main use of a per-request Choice, needs.
